title_en: Endangered Parrot Eggs Hatch After Airport Smuggling Arrest
title_zh: 鹦鹉蛋在机场走私者被捕后孵化
summary_zh: 上周，南非约翰内斯堡机场截获五十枚疑似濒危鹦鹉蛋，一名泰国籍嫌疑人因涉嫌使用自制孵化袋随身携带走私被捕。部分蛋已孵化，雏鸟正在接受密集照护。调查表明这些蛋属于受《濒危野生动植物种国际贸易公约》保护的鹦鹉物种。此案与七月另一宗走私418枚鹦鹉蛋案件共同凸显了跨境野生动物走私网络的复杂性，南非正通过跨部门协作打击此类非法贸易。
reading_passage:
Staff at the National Zoological Garden in Pretoria have been looking after the eggs and hatchlings

Fifty eggs suspected to be those of endangered parrots were intercepted at South Africa's main airport in Johannesburg last Thursday - and some of them have now hatched.

A 50-year-old Thai national was arrested for allegedly attempting to smuggle them in a "homemade incubator bag" carried as hand luggage, according to the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE).

Many of the rescued eggs have successfully hatched, with the chicks now receiving "intensive" care to "maximise their chances of survival", it added.

If convicted, the suspected wildlife trafficker faces a fine of up to 10m rand ($626,000, £461,000) or up to 10 years in prison, or both.

Initial investigations suggest the eggs belong to a parrot species protected under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (Cites).

The arrest followed a joint operation by the DFFE, the Green Scorpions - a specialised environmental enforcement unit - and various divisions of the police.

Environment Minister David Maynier has congratulated all the agencies involved, saying "illegal wildlife trafficking can only be challenged by a co-ordinated defence of our natural heritage".

He particularly thanked the dedicated staff at the National Zoological Garden in the capital, Pretoria, "who have been working tirelessly to incubate the seized eggs and provide specialised care to the hatchlings".

Last Thursday's arrest follows that of a 23-year-old Thai citizen in July, also caught at Johannesburg's OR Tambo International Airport, who was attempting to smuggle 418 parrot eggs.

The arrests highlighted the growing sophistication of transnational wildlife trafficking networks and reinforced "the importance of co-ordinated, intelligence-led law enforcement efforts", the DFFE said.

The illegal collection and trafficking of parrot eggs posed "a serious threat to wild bird populations and animal welfare", it added.

Officials explained that such eggs were often smuggled in improvised incubators and in conditions that endangered the welfare of developing embryos and hatchlings.

Wildlife trafficking remains a major threat in South Africa, one of the world's most biodiverse countries, with criminal networks frequently targeting animals such as elephants and pangolins, for sale on the international black market.

To combat the threat, the country adopted a new strategy six years ago to strengthen collaboration between government institutions, law enforcement agencies, conservation authorities, customs officials, prosecutors and international partners to dismantle criminal networks involved in the illicit wildlife trade.

Customs officers intercepted a large number of rare eggs before they could be smuggled abroad.

difficult_sentences.sentence: Fifty eggs suspected to be those of endangered parrots were intercepted at South Africa's main airport in Johannesburg last Thursday - and some of them have now hatched.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句为 `Fifty eggs ... were intercepted ... and some of them have now hatched`；`suspected to be those of endangered parrots` 是过去分词短语作后置定语，相当于非限制性定语从句 `which were suspected to be...`；破折号后的并列分句补充后续结果。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 过去分词短语作后置定语；破折号连接的并列结构
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 上周四，在南非约翰内斯堡的主要机场，五十枚疑似濒危鹦鹉蛋被截获，其中一些现已孵化。

difficult_sentences.sentence: Many of the rescued eggs have successfully hatched, with the chicks now receiving "intensive" care to "maximise their chances of survival", it added.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句为 `Many of the rescued eggs have successfully hatched`；`with the chicks now receiving "intensive" care` 是 “with + 名词 + 现在分词” 的独立主格结构，表示伴随情况；`to "maximise their chances of survival"` 是目的状语。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: with 独立主格结构；不定式作目的状语
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 许多获救的蛋已成功孵化，雏鸟目前正接受“强化”照护，以“最大限度提高存活几率”，该部门补充道。

difficult_sentences.sentence: Last Thursday's arrest follows that of a 23-year-old Thai citizen in July, also caught at Johannesburg's OR Tambo International Airport, who was attempting to smuggle 418 parrot eggs.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句为 `Last Thursday's arrest follows that of a 23-year-old Thai citizen in July`，其中 `that` 替代 `the arrest`；`also caught at ...` 是过去分词短语作非限制性后置定语；`who was attempting ...` 是非限制性定语从句修饰先行词 `citizen`。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 代词 that 的替代；过去分词短语与定语从句作后置定语
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 上周四的逮捕行动紧随7月一名23岁泰国公民被捕之后，该人同样在约翰内斯堡的奥利弗·坦博国际机场被捕，当时正试图走私418枚鹦鹉蛋。

difficult_sentences.sentence: To combat the threat, the country adopted a new strategy six years ago to strengthen collaboration between government institutions, law enforcement agencies, conservation authorities, customs officials, prosecutors and international partners to dismantle criminal networks involved in the illicit wildlife trade.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句为 `the country adopted a new strategy six years ago`；句首的 `To combat the threat` 是目的状语；`to strengthen ... and international partners` 是第二个目的状语；`to dismantle criminal networks involved in the illicit wildlife trade` 是第三个目的状语，其中 `involved in the illicit wildlife trade` 是过去分词短语作后置定语修饰 `networks`。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 多个不定式目的状语；过去分词短语作定语
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 为应对这一威胁，该国六年前通过了一项新战略，以加强政府机构、执法部门、保护机构、海关官员、检察官及国际伙伴之间的协作，从而捣毁参与非法野生动物贸易的犯罪网络。

idioms.usage_note: 通常与介词 `on` 连用，如 `on the black market`，指在非法渠道中买卖。
idioms.example: Many stolen animal products are sold on the black market.

idioms.usage_note: 常见于正式或新闻语境，表示用一物替代另一物；后面直接接名词或名词短语。
idioms.example: Poachers sometimes target hippo teeth in place of ivory.

idioms.usage_note: 常用于新闻报道，指某一活动或问题的新的、尚未充分管控的范围。
idioms.example: Rare plant smuggling has become the new frontier of wildlife trafficking.

reading_questions.question: What is the main subject of the article?

options.A: A campaign to ban parrot ownership in South Africa.
options.B: A scientific study of parrot breeding in captivity.
options.C: A dispute between South Africa and Thailand over trade policy.
options.D: The interception and hatching of endangered parrot eggs linked to wildlife trafficking.

reading_questions.question: According to the first paragraph, who has been looking after the eggs and hatchlings?

options.A: Officials at the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment.
options.C: Staff at the National Zoological Garden in Pretoria.
options.D: Customs officers at OR Tambo International Airport.

reading_questions.question: What can be inferred about the eggs from their discovery in a "homemade incubator bag" carried as hand luggage?

options.A: They were destined for a zoo breeding programme.
options.B: They had already hatched before being packed.
options.C: They were being transported in conditions intended to keep them alive for hatching.
options.D: They were being sent to a laboratory for genetic testing.

reading_questions.question: In paragraph 4, the word "intensive" in "intensive care" most nearly means:
Which best describes the author's attitude toward the wildlife trafficking case?

options.A: Critical of South Africa's conservation agencies.
options.B: Indifferent to the fate of the eggs.
options.D: Factual and measured, highlighting both the threat and the need for coordinated action.

reading_questions.question: How does the article organize its information?

options.A: It first compares different endangered species in South Africa, then explains how CITES works.
options.B: It begins with the rescue and care of eggs, then details the arrest and legal context, and finally discusses broader wildlife trafficking challenges and strategies.
options.C: It presents a chronological history of Thai bird smuggling since 2020.
options.D: It introduces a government policy debate, then interviews conservationists for their opinions.

reading_questions.question: Which title best fits the article?

options.B: "Endangered Parrot Eggs Hatch After Airport Smuggling Arrest"
options.D: "Zoo Staff Celebrate Rare Parrot Breeding Success"

sources.title: Parrot eggs hatch after suspected Thai smuggler arrested at South African airport
